key_insight: LongBanana introduces an expert-designed and expert-verified benchmark for testing whether AI can combine evidence from many reference images into one coherent image. It evaluates visual reasoning and reference handling, not just image quality.
problem_solved: Multi-reference image generation requires AI to find relevant visual details across a long context, ignore distractors, and correctly combine entities and their relationships in the final image.
method: Construct 90 carefully designed tasks organized using a 3-by-3 taxonomy.
Provide about 32 reference images per task, requiring retrieval of dispersed visual evidence and rejection of distractors.
Use expert-designed and expert-verified tasks to assess entity and relationship binding in coherent final-image synthesis.
impact: LongBanana gives practitioners a structured benchmark for evaluating long-context, multi-reference image synthesis. It can help reveal failures in evidence selection and composition that visual quality alone may miss.
visual_elements: Reference-to-output pipeline: many reference images → evidence selection → one synthesized image.
3-by-3 task grid showing the benchmark structure, without inventing unspecified category labels.
Reference-image collage with relevant evidence highlighted and distractors crossed out.
Entity-and-relationship diagram connecting selected visual details to the final composition.
paper_title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
paper_authors: Haoxiang Cao, Yuxuan Zhang, Penghui Du, Bo Li, Jiajiong Cao
